items.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 18 at 1:20PM PST until November 18 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Francisco Bay Shoreline, The Central
Coast, The Santa Clara Valley and Eastern Hills, and The Santa Cruz
Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Wind gusts up to 70 mph will be possible in
the higher terrain.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 1:16PM PST until November 18 at 4:15PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Monterey County

* WHEN...Until 415 PM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 115 PM PST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. This  will
cause urban and small stream flooding. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of
rain has fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Seaside, Monterey, Marina, Tassajara Hot Springs, Arroyo Seco,
Jamesburg, Lucia, Gorda, Big Sur Village, Pacific Grove,
Carmel-By-The-Sea, Carmel Valley Village, Sycamore Flat, Esalen
Institute, Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park, Partington Ridge,
Colman Canyon, Cachagua Near The Los Padres Dam, San Clemente Dam
and Pico Blanco Campground.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 8:08AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13
to 17 ft. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18
to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored breakpoints along the
coast from this afternoon through Friday morning.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.
items.instruction:
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

items.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued November 18 at 4:46AM PST until November 19 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
are possible over the Plaskett and Timber burn areas.

* WHERE...For the Timber Scar, portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los
Padres National Forecast from Andrew Molera State Park to
Partington Ridge including the town of Big Sur.

For the Plaskett Scar, areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile
marker 11 including Los Burros Road.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas is
expected during the watch period. Residents near the Timber burn
area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the
drainages within Lafler, Castro, and Graves Canyons, as well as
drainages between Grimes and Castro Canyons.

Residents near the Plaskett burn area should prepare for potential
debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and Prewitt Creeks.

Be sure to stay up to date with information from local authorities.
Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas,
roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas, which may lead
to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Big Sur, Plaskett, and Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Local emergency services are monitoring the situation and will issue
a public statement as conditions warrant. PLAN NOW so you will know
what to do in an emergency. Keep informed by listening to local radio
and television for statements and possible warnings. Follow the
advice of public safety officials.
